objectives: Recognise the gn spelling at the start of taught words.
Identify /n/ as the first spoken sound in taught gn words.
Distinguish gn words from words beginning with /g/ or /n/ alone.
Use the whole word to confirm sound and spelling.
concepts: In these taught initial gn words, g is silent.
The spelling keeps g before n even though g is not pronounced.
The rest of the word distinguishes gnat and gnaw.

definitions.definition: A written letter that is not pronounced.
A letter or group of letters representing a sound.
A speech sound that can distinguish one word from another.

workedExamples.solution: The word begins with /n/; the g is silent.
Gnat begins with /n/; gap begins with /g/.
The first spoken sound is /n/, not /g/.

commonMistakes: Pronouncing g in initial gn words.
Deleting g from the spelling because it is silent.
Guessing without listening to the first sound.
keyTakeaways: Initial g is silent in the taught gn words.
Check the rest of the word.
revisionPoints: g is silent in initial gn.
